turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I guess what brought me in is... I just don't feel like myself anymore. I barely talk to people. I just go flat and quiet. It's like, even getting started on my cleaning route at work feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. 

And I know all about pushing carts, I'm a janitor over at the municipal building. We have this one cart, the big grey utility one, and the front left wheel has been stuck for a month. It pulls hard to the left. I keep telling the day-shift supervisor about it, but he just ignores me. He always wears these ridiculous bright yellow ties, I have no idea why. I took some business and management classes back in community college, so I know a thing or two about how a workplace is supposed to be run, and you don't just leave broken equipment for your night crew. I always thought I'd be the one sitting at the desk wearing the tie, not emptying the trash bins for guys like him. 

But... I don't know. I don't even have the energy to argue with him about the wheel anymore. I just stay quiet. I don't really have the words for anybody lately. Everything just feels too heavy.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, actually. It's mostly when I'm mopping after hours. The building is usually totally empty, you know? But I'll hear this man's voice. He says my name, or he'll tell me I missed a spot. It's so clear, it sounds just like he's standing right over by the stairwell. But then I look, and... nobody. Just the stairs. 

Those stairs are a real pain to keep clean, by the way. They put in this textured rubber treading about five years ago, supposed to be slip-resistant, which I guess it is, but it traps every single piece of grit and dirt from people's shoes. Especially in the winter with the rock salt. You can't just sweep it, you really have to get in there with a stiff brush. I brought in a specialized brush I bought with my own money from the hardware store on 4th street—the one owned by that guy whose son went to high school with my nephew. Nice kid, played baseball. Anyway, I tried telling the day-shift supervisor we needed better supplies for those stairs, but like I said, he just ignores me. Probably too busy adjusting his yellow tie. But yeah, the voice... it's just really clear, but nobody's ever there.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard that voice during a time when you were not feeling depressed?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually... there was a stretch of several weeks, not too long ago, where my mood had lifted some. I was getting through my work a little better, and I was actually eating my meals again. I usually just pack a ham sandwich, but during those weeks I started going to that diner on 5th street for my break. They have this meatloaf special on Thursdays. You wouldn't think diner meatloaf is anything special, but they use this brown sugar and ketchup glaze. My mother used to make a glaze just like it when I was a kid. She'd put it in the oven and the whole house would smell like it. She always used this heavy glass Pyrex dish with the little handles on the side... 

But anyway, what I mean is, even when I was feeling better like that, getting through my shifts and going to the diner, I still heard the voice saying my name in the stairwell. And I stayed completely convinced that the hallway cameras were being used to track me. They put those new dome cameras in last year, and the contractor who installed them left drywall dust everywhere. I had to clean it all up myself, and let me tell you, drywall dust completely ruins a standard vacuum filter. You need a specialized HEPA filter or the fine dust just blows right back out the exhaust into the air, which completely defeats the whole purpose of vacuuming in the first place. I tried explaining that to the supervisor, but you know how that goes.

turns.patient_response:
Yeah, the depression part... that's been with me for about a year and two months now. It started up not long after the move, actually, so definitely before the voices began. 

Moving is just terrible at my age, you know? I had to pack up all these boxes myself. I bought those heavy-duty ones from the hardware store, but honestly, the packing tape they sell nowadays doesn't stick worth a darn. You tape up the bottom, put in a few heavy things, and the whole bottom just gives out. I have this collection of old encyclopedias from when I took some community college classes back in the 80s. I thought I was going to be a history teacher for a while. Obviously, that didn't pan out, but I couldn't bear to throw the books away. They weigh an absolute ton, though. I think I pulled a muscle in my lower back just getting them into the rental truck. The guy at the U-Haul place was supposed to reserve a dolly for me, but when I got there they were completely out, so I had to carry every single box by hand up to the new place. 

But yeah, right after I got settled in there, that's when the really heavy, down feeling started. Every day, most of the day, just... stuck like that. Long before I ever heard anyone in the stairwell.

Those cameras, I tell you, they have this little red light that blinks when they're recording, or at least that's what the manual says. I found a PDF of the manual online one night when I couldn't sleep. The internet is funny like that, you can find the instruction manual for just about anything if you look hard enough. I ended up reading about how they manufacture the glass for those camera domes. It's supposed to be scratch-resistant, but the maintenance guys wipe them down with paper towels, which is the worst thing you can do. Paper towels are made of wood pulp, so they leave these microscopic scratches on the plastic or glass, and over time it gets all cloudy. You're supposed to use a microfiber cloth. I bought a whole pack of them at the auto parts store. They were on sale, buy one get one free. I gave a few to my neighbor, he drives this old Buick that he's always polishing... 

But yeah, to answer your question, yes. Even during those weeks when I wasn't feeling depressed at all, the voice in the stairwell and the cameras watching me... that didn't stop. It just kept right on going.
